paper.title: HKOI 2006 Heat Event — Junior Group FITB

prompt.en: The following program segment swaps the values of two integer variables x and y. Fill in the blank.

targets.source: int f(int x, int y) { x = y - x; y = y - x; return {{A}}; }

prompt.en: Given integers n and m (-1000 < n < 1000 and 0 < m < 1000), the following program computes the smallest non-negative integer x such that n-x is divisible by m. For example, if n = 12, m = 5, then x = 2. Fill in the blank.

targets.source: int f(int n, int m) { return {{B}}; }

prompt.en: You are given a function max3(a, b, c) which returns the maximum of three integers a, b and c (0 < a, b, c < 10000). The following function returns the minimum of a, b and c. Fill in the blank using max3.

targets.source: int min3(int a, int b, int c) { return {{C}}; }
targets.helperSource: int max3(int a, int b, int c) { int m = a; if (b > m) m = b; if (c > m) m = c; return m; }

prompt.en: The following function returns the median of a, b and c. Fill in the blank using max3 and min3.

targets.source: int median3(int a, int b, int c) { return {{D}}; }
targets.helperSource:
int max3(int a, int b, int c) { int m = a; if (b > m) m = b; if (c > m) m = c; return m; }
int min3(int a, int b, int c) { int m = a; if (b < m) m = b; if (c < m) m = c; return m; }

prompt.en: The following program reads 100 positive integers (each less than 10000) from the input and outputs them in ascending order. Fill in the blank.

targets.source: int F[10001],i,j,temp; int bump(){F[temp]={{E}};return F[temp];} int f(int value,int times,int initial){temp=value;F[temp]=initial;for(i=1;i<=times;i++)bump();return F[temp];}

prompt.en: Chris has an unlimited number of \$4 and \$7 coins. However, some amounts cannot be paid with only \$4 and \$7 coins. Examples are \$1, \$2, \$3 and \$5. List all other integral amounts that cannot be paid.
Let S(n, a) = 1+a+a²+…+aⁿ. The following program calculates the value of S(n, a). Making use of the fact S(n, a) = 1 + a × S(n-1, a), fill in the blank.

targets.source: int f(int n, int a) { int i, ans=1; for(i=1;i<=n;i++) ans={{G}}; return ans; }

prompt.en: The following program computes all prime numbers less than 1000 using Sieve of Eratosthenes, i.e. by repeatedly crossing out multiples of prime numbers. Fill in the blanks.

targets.source:
#include <stdio.h>
int main() { int n,i,j,marked[1000]; scanf("%d",&n); for(i=1;i<1000;i++) marked[i]=0; for(i=2;i<=n;i++) if(!marked[i]) { printf("%d is prime\n",i); for({{H}};j++) marked[i*j]=1; } return 0; }
